topic: Subject as a second NP function
claim: Every Type I genitive is assigned both determiner and subject function.
evidence_summary: Semantic parallels survive changes of function. Local reflexive antecedence supplies independent evidence, but a post-head by-phrase can also antecede a reflexive.
finding: Test whether binding or control tracks genitive position when participant role and discourse perspective are held constant.
traditional_parallel: P. 248 keeps the recipient role distinct from indirect-object function when the recipient is expressed in a PP. A genitive and a clausal subject likewise can share a role across different constructions. A methodological inconsistency would require comparable independent evidence: local binding, constituent position and control in NPs need their own tests.
inference: What evidence for a genitive’s role as determiner independently establishes a second function as subject?

evidence.source: Jeffrey T. Runner, Rachel S. Sussman & Michael K. Tanenhaus (2003). Assignment of reference to reflexives and pronouns in picture noun phrases: Evidence from eye movements. Cognition 89(1), B1–B13.
evidence.passage: §16.5.1, p. 472. Every Type I genitive is assigned both determiner and subject function.
evidence.example: In the two conditions, .35 and .27 of reflexive responses selected the clause subject, while .65 and .72 selected the possessor.
evidence.establishes: A possessor has a substantial advantage in these picture NPs, but another antecedent is available. These data do not settle subjecthood for genitives of event nouns.
